title: specgen: let --cap-add extend the capabilities required by the image
body:
`--cap-add` is ignored for any image that sets the `io.containers.capabilities` label. `podman run --cap-add SYS_ADMIN quay.io/podman/stable` starts the container without CAP_SYS_ADMIN, while the same flag works on an image without the label.

In `pkg/specgen/generate/security_linux.go`, the label's list is normalised into `capsRequired` and, when the container is allowed to have all of it, assigned to `caplist`, replacing the set already collected from the default capabilities plus `s.CapAdd`. The flag's entries are dropped there. Luap99's comment on the issue says a user who asks for more should be able to set it, so the fix merges the user's request into the label's list instead of replacing it. An image that lists no capabilities, or one asking for a capability outside the default set, behaves as before.

The capability handling moved into its own function so it can be exercised without a runtime; nothing else about it changed.

Fixes #30269

Verified: `go test -run TestSetupCapabilities ./pkg/specgen/generate/`. The new case fails before the change — bounding set comes out as `CAP_SETGID,CAP_SETUID` — and passes after it: `CAP_SETGID,CAP_SETUID,CAP_SYS_ADMIN`. `go test ./pkg/specgen/generate/` passes. `gofmt` and `go vet` are clean; `golangci-lint` is not installed on this machine, so `make validatepr` was not run.
